correctness.rationale: Definitions and the eight closures are given exactly by the binary antimorphisms R and E. Intermediate word lengths 1,2,5,12,22,46,90,182 are recomputed from the directive. The six indexed positions meet all 12608 nonempty distinct factors by direct exhaustive interval enumeration. For the lower bound, twelve explicit present factors have precisely twelve maximal coverage-incidence masks; all 792 five-mask combinations fail to cover every obstruction factor. Since every position is dominated by one maximal incidence mask, no attractor of size five or fewer exists. The standalone Python standard-library checker on the exact delivered file reproduces every step; finite exhaustion is complete at length 182 and no infinite inference is made.

value.rationale: The 2024 primary paper makes the uniform-attractor bound for binary generalized pseudostandard prefixes an explicit research problem, and an intervening published example excludes the bound four by attaining five. A rigorously verified size-six prefix also rules out the next universal bound five, giving a stronger structural obstruction for this natural low-complexity word family. Twelve explicitly exhibited factor constraints and a twelve-column covering reduction explain and reproducibly certify the failure of five points. The finding is a motivated finite threshold for a natural invariant, not an arbitrary sample; it does not claim length minimality or infer unboundedness.
